answer.rationale: Rollback is unavailable: compliance forbids reverting the security patch. Circuit breaking would fail customer writes and conflicts with the objective. Regional failover has no supporting signal and would put in-flight settlement writes at risk. The live constraint is write-path p99 at 5x during peak, write-heavy settlement. memory_b3 is the closest playbook for absorbing surge without dropping writes, but it describes headroom provisioned before a known peak, not mid-incident, so it may not transfer cleanly. memory_b5 recovered transactional write latency by moving report/dashboard reads off the primary, but current load is described as write-heavy, so replica routing may miss the bottleneck. Prefer add_capacity as a standard scale-out that keeps writes accepted. Verifying b3 and b5 to test the before-vs-during mismatch and whether the write-latency pattern was actually read-contention. Residual uncertainty: the new release may have raised write cost rather than raw capacity demand.
